title: Sikemux · a whole team of AI coders, in one window
excerpt: Out of Claude? The chat carries on in Codex. Sikemux is a free, MIT-licensed native app for Mac and Linux that runs Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents on your own plans and shows which one needs you.
content_html:
Claude Code, Codex and more, side by side in one native app. See who’s working, who’s stuck and who needs you.

Apple Silicon Mac and Linux · 31.9 MB · free, MIT

  • Your subscriptions. Claude Code, Codex and five more, on the subscriptions you already have.

  • Native, not Electron. Drawn on the GPU. The whole app downloads at 31.9 MB.

  • Agents that talk. They message each other, hand off work and ask only what's yours to decide.

  • Answer from anywhere. The MacBook notch asks for you. Away from the desk, your phone does.

How it fits

No AI of its own.
It runs yours.

Install an agent the usual way and sign in. Sikemux finds it and starts it with your login, on this computer or any host you link.

Watch and answer from the app, the notch or your phone.

Carry on

Out of Claude?
The chat carries on in Codex.

Start an agent next to your code. It reads the project, edits files and runs commands while you watch. When one plan runs dry, the same chat carries on with another agent.

Every project
gets a chief.

Tell @Chief what you want. It hands the work to Claude Code, Codex and your other agents, answers what it can, and brings you only the calls that need you.

What is Sikemux, in one sentence?

A Mac app where you work on a project together with AI coding agents: they write and test the code, and you watch, review and ship, without juggling an editor, terminals, Git and a browser in separate apps.

Which agents does it work with?

Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode, OMP and Grok. Install one the usual way and sign in, and Sikemux finds it and starts it with your own login.

Does Sikemux send my code to a model?

No. Sikemux has no AI of its own. Your code only goes to the agent you choose, through that agent's own account. Some agents can also use an API key you add in Settings, but you never need one.

Linux, Windows, Intel Macs?

Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 11 or later, and Linux on x86_64 and arm64 as a .deb, AppImage or Arch package. The Linux app needs Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13 or newer; on older systems, install only the core with --host. Windows and Intel Macs can build it from source, but there's no download for them yet. Join the Discord or watch the GitHub repository to hear when there is.

Is it free?

Yes. Sikemux is free and MIT-licensed, and it needs no account on your own computer. It runs the Claude Code, Codex and other subscriptions you already pay for, or free models if you have none. We don't resell models or take a cut.

How does it stay alive?

Nothing is for sale today. Sikemux is built by people who use it all day. If we charge later, it will be for things that cost us money to run, such as a machine we host for your agents, sync between your computers, and team features. The app you download stays free and MIT, and the licence means nobody can take that back, us included.

How it fits

No AI of its own.It runs yours.

What is Sikemux, in one sentence?

A Mac app where you work on a project together with AI coding agents: they write and test the code, and you watch, review and ship, without juggling an editor, terminals, Git and a browser in separate apps.

Which agents does it work with?

Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode, OMP and Grok. Install one the usual way and sign in, and Sikemux finds it and starts it with your own login.

Does Sikemux send my code to a model?

No. Sikemux has no AI of its own. Your code only goes to the agent you choose, through that agent's own account. Some agents can also use an API key you add in Settings, but you never need one.

Linux, Windows, Intel Macs?

Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 11 or later, and Linux on x86_64 and arm64 as a .deb, AppImage or Arch package. The Linux app needs Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13 or newer; on older systems, install only the core with --host. Windows and Intel Macs can build it from source, but there's no download for them yet. Join the Discord or watch the GitHub repository to hear when there is.

Is it free?

是的。 Sikemux is free and MIT-licensed, and it needs no account on your own computer. It runs the Claude Code, Codex and other subscriptions you already pay for, or free models if you have none. We don't resell models or take a cut.

How does it stay alive?

Nothing is for sale today. Sikemux is built by people who use it all day. If we charge later, it will be for things that cost us money to run, such as a machine we host for your agents, sync between your computers, and team features. The app you download stays free and MIT, and the licence means nobody can take that back, us included.
